## Design

### 2026-11-06: After _a lot_ of trial and error, I decided on the layout of LEDs on the board. Each node in this graph represents an LED and a letter. The colour of a node represents the last element to reach that l

**2.5h**

After _a lot_ of trial and error, I decided on the layout of LEDs on the board. Each node in this graph represents an LED and a letter. The colour of a node represents the last element to reach that letter. The path from the root node to a letter is the elements needed in that order for the letter.

![Graph](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/e9abf928c972851950459076247452878b12318eff1d5354de3e6b090c902cbf.png)

As you can see, the nodes are in a grid, with vertical and horizontal edges connecting them. The root node is the middle and the nodes are horizontally symmetric around it. The root node will be controlled by a button below it.

The total number of LEDs is 28: 26 for the letters, 1 for the button indicator and 1 for the status indicator. The LEDs will all be RGB so I can make different colours have different meanings.

I did some research and reading to decide that I'll use WS2812Bs (package 5050) for the LEDs. They are 5mm x 5mm which is hopefully manageable for me to solder on, despite being SMDs.

The MCU chip I'll be using is the RP2040. I narrowed it down to either the Waveshare RP2040, the XIAO RP2040 v1.0, or the XIAO RP2040 Plus. After some consideration and learning about the differences in cost, size, and GPIOs, I decided on the XIAO RP2040 v1.0.

![RP2040](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/d9b15ee64176e814a5badd00be8059cea7c085c2067e0ea4e8a7127d8b456520.png)

I sourced the components needed and made a BOM, excluding the PCB:

![BOM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/ba723f8f1f90da598f1013eaee83f67c0440ec2b7a84ab59a41fc439f0a75048.png)

The goal is to have a very compact board, with the LEDs and one button on one side and the MCU and other buttons on the other side.

### 2026-11-07: Big progress today. First, I designed the schematic based on the plans I made previously. Here's what it looks like:

**4.52h**

Big progress today. First, I designed the schematic based on the plans I made previously. Here's what it looks like:

![Schematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/34e4ef5a5ba033f8cbb46b57866214aad303083c69a290499d22584744a94f21.png)

I quite like how it turned out and I think I've made it very neat if I do say so myself.

Next was the hard part: Laying out the board. First, I planned the arrangement with accurate dimensions in Affinity. This also includes some experimenting with what the silkscreen graphics would look like:

![Layout plan](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/776bbce4e8fcb421a4df36dbb50b52e9a15ea192844dbf154d6a9cc0143335d6.png)

Then, after a few hours of work, I replicated the whole design on the board. I also added most of the silkscreen graphics too. Here's what the final board I made looks like:

![Board](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/4d340f46a6451435c58141783632da66d28b27fe86297d90ad4035b9f01480a5.png)

![PCB Front](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/0597483e4bbb48f43641f22a1d0bf88b1dba029e3c82c893e43910209d12ade3.png)

![PCB Back](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/245e1bc044fbe19265f4cd461df0a68611e422642aecf32542f6bc860d071e62.png)

Next I'll add more graphics to the back of the board, since it's a little bare right now. Then I'll do the routing.
